body:
I just checked out "Code 3" and, man, it was a trip. I was expecting a typical comedy with Rainn Wilson, but this was surprisingly heavy. It follows two totally burned-out paramedics and a rookie over one crazy 24-hour shift, and it's a lot.

What hit me was the authenticity-it really shows how tough the EMS job is. It doesn't shy away from the dark stuff, mixing some truly raw, emotional drama with moments of seriously dark humor. That constant tonal shift works, though. One minute you're laughing at their gallows humor, and the next you're totally punched in the gut by a tragic call.

Wilson's performance as Randy is fantastic; you really feel his exhaustion and cynicism. He nails the snappy, fourth-wall breaking narration that clues you into the messed-up healthcare system. It's a bummer that the rookie character felt a bit generic, like just a foil for Randy.

And it seems like an original story, co-written by a former paramedic, which makes sense why it feels so real.

Is it worth watching? Absolutely. It's a compelling look at first responders. It's not just a comedy; it's a solid drama with real heart and respect for the people doing this impossible job. Go see it.

I used to work in EMS. The dark humour in this is very accurate but if you're looking for a belly-laughs comedy then this is not the film you want. It is a really good portrait of a crew and their work, with lots of details that show the writers know the subject, but it doesn't get stuck on procedural stuff and is really about the people.

Well what was advertised by its trailer and from the depiction of the movie poster I really expected a daft comedy full of silly one liners and gags. Never judge a book by it's cover. This one really surprised me, to the point I'm knocked back a bit.

I'm a fan of both Rainn Wilson and Lil Rey Howery primarily for their supporting roles in comedy movies. I still never really see either of them as leading men, but I do enjoy some of their roles. So my expectations for this were realistically very low. I've seen little to no promotion on this movie so I expected a below average comedy. Ive never been so glad to be wrong.

This is not a comedy by normal standards, I meen I can see why it can be described as a dark comedy but it's also quite surprisingly a heart warming drama and also very surprising to me was that it's terrifyingly realistic. I'm from the UK and sadly this movie relates to what's happening here. The health care service is under dire need of help. This movie addresses that and then some. Working stupidly long hours with little to no thanks in a broken system.

This movie shows the life's of two paramedics and a student in what I would normally consider the worst shift ever, but this is not the worst shift ever. It's a average day. They fight amongst each other and in their own heads as they are at times fighting a losing battle trying to find the light at the end of the tunnel. They are underappreciated and at times forget what humanity is because all they see is the worst of situations and the worst of people.

Rainn gives one of, if not the best performance of his career. I was also hugely impressed by Lil Rey, in fact all the performances. Very strong movie. This i believe maybe the first movie I've seen of young actress Aimee Carrero, but a really great performance and hopefully a actress to keep an eye on in the future.

Honestly, nothing makes me happier than finding a sweet gem like this of which I had no expectations. Really surprised me, shame they didn't promote it a bit more. And hopefully it does garner a respectable following. Really good movie, highly recommend it.

Really hope you guys check it out if you already haven't and enjoy.

I was a little hesitant to watch this, as Rainn Wilson has been in some rather odd and uninspired movies, with more misses than hits.

I'm glad to report this is probably his best work yet. He plays a paramedic, expressing his life both in his role and wall breaking monologues.

I'd be hesitant classifying it as a comedy, though. There are maybe a couple chuckle moments, but it's mostly a drama, leaving you frustrated with the state of the system at times. Even so, it's an important message to spread, and I was ultimately glad to have watched.

Pleasantly surprised watching this movie. Didn't have expectations but this definitely exceeded my expectations and I'm sure it would do for you as well. A very realistic movie, with subtle humor, catchy dialogues, nice screenplay and good acting.

You'll never get bored. 90 minutes well spent over the weekend!
